context.summary: Greenfield internal image asset tool for five users; React is preferred, Python is required for OpenCV and AI image workflows, SEO is not required, and deployment is one Linux server.

architecture.reason: One small team owns one product and no capability requires an independent deployment lifecycle.

selected.reason: It preserves the team's existing preference for an interactive private UI.
evidence: The application is an authenticated internal tool.

basis: UI mode, SEO boundary, and team preference are explicit.

selected.reason: A client SPA does not need an SSR server or framework caching model.
evidence: SEO and SSR are explicitly out of scope.

basis: The rendering boundary clearly favors a simple SPA build.

selected.reason: It keeps the API in the Python runtime already required by media processing.
evidence: OpenCV and AI image workflows require Python.
The product needs an HTTP API.

basis: The required domain ecosystem creates a large candidate gap.

selected.reason: Relational asset, project, user, and job metadata fit one transactional source of truth.
evidence: No specialized database workload is present.

basis: A single relational database covers current access patterns.

selected.reason: Private deployment benefits from an S3-compatible binary-storage boundary.
evidence: Generated and uploaded images should not be database blobs.

basis: A managed S3 service would be simpler if public cloud is allowed.

selected.reason: Image generation and transformation must execute outside request latency; Redis is justified only as the broker.

basis: Expected job volume is unknown, so database-backed jobs remain credible.

selected.reason: It is broker infrastructure for the selected worker, not a speculative application cache.
evidence: The recommendation explicitly requires a queue broker.

basis: Database jobs may remove the broker at the initial job volume.

selected.reason: It operates the web, API, worker, database, broker, and storage processes on one server without a cluster control plane.

alternatives.reason: Prefer this if initial retries and throughput remain modest.
Prefer this if public cloud is allowed and reduced operations outweigh provider dependence.

rejected.reason: No replayable stream or multiple consumer-group requirement.
Single-server deployment has no orchestration requirement.
One team and one deployment lifecycle favor a modular monolith.

overengineering.reason: Used as a queue broker, not an application cache.
Multi-node HA and platform operations are absent.

risks: Self-hosted MinIO and Redis require backup and monitoring.
Job volume is not yet measured.

scaling_triggers.condition: queue latency breaches the product target after worker tuning
scaling_triggers.evaluate: a managed queue or horizontally scaled workers

scaling_triggers.condition: multi-node high availability becomes a current requirement

changes: Use the selected modular monolith and one server.
Change the queue or deployment only when its trigger is observed.
